https://www.autoweek.com/racing/formula-.text: World Champion Lando Norris finally snapped Mercedes’ unbeaten streak in qualifying this season by snatching pole position for Formula 1’s Hungarian Grand Prix.Kimi Antonelli and George Russell had fronted every Grand Prix qualifying session so far in 2026 for Mercedes, but the layout of the Hungaroring has not played to the W17’s strengths.Drivers were also struggling for consistency on a partially resurfaced track that has been slightly breaking up at some corners.A mistake on his first push lap in Q3 cost McLaren driver Norris time but he made amends on his second lap to clock a time of 1:17.207s, beating Lewis Hamilton by a mere 0.012s.It was Norris’ 17th pole of his career and his second at the Hungaroring.“It’s been a while, and I felt confident all weekend, so nice to be able to turn it into something,” Norris said.Hamilton’s second place was provisional owing to the Ferrari driver clearly impeding Oscar Piastri on the McLaren driver’s hot lap—and as expected it came with a three-place grid penalty. Hamilton will start instead P5, Piastri in third.Both Ferrari drivers rued scruffy laps, having not improved at the end, with a “disappointed” third-placed (promoted to P2) Charles Leclerc describing his session as “messy,” as the team’s wait for a first pole of the year goes on.Antonelli also was tagged with a post-qualifying penalty, with stewards having determined the Mercedes driver failed to slow sufficiently for yellow flags brought out when Red Bull’s Max Verstappen spun in Q3. Antonelli will line up seventh, gaining a spot for Hamilton’s penalty while losing three places for his own. That puts Russell in sixth, the Briton’s session slightly compromised by a minor water leak at the end which meant it was “like a water pistol being sprayed at the tires.”“The whole weekend we haven’t had the pace, we’ve looked strong in race pace, did we strike the right balance between quali and race set-up we’ll find tomorrow, but we struggled to get the tires switched on all day,” Russell said.Antonelli agreed that “we were a bit out of the window with tires, in Q3 we made a good step, the car finally felt a bit more alive,” but he rued an ill-timed yellow flag that he reckoned may have cost him one spot.Red Bull endured a troubled session, with both Verstappen and Isack Hadjar having a spin en route to sixth and eighth respectively.“The whole weekend has been tough but in qualifying especially the car is just degrading, we don’t have tire degradation, we have car degradation,” Verstappen said. “I can’t make anything [any sense] out if it, it’s very tough, the car just suddenly started oversteering a lot, every lap I did got worse and worse. Not good.”Fernando Alonso delivered hope for Aston Martin as, a week after being two seconds down on the nearest car, the Spaniard made it through to Q2.Alonso qualified in 16th place, putting the Aston Martin as the ninth-best car, faster than the struggling Williams team and new tail-enders Cadillac.FORMULA 1 AWS HUNGARIAN GRAND PRIX 2026—PROVISIONAL STARTING GRID Hungaroring—Budapest, Hungary , July 26, 2026 Pos/Driver/Team/Qualifying Time1. By Newsfile September 5, 2026 at 4:03 p.m. Warsaw, Poland–(Newsfile Corp. – September 5, 2026) – IFIORA has announced that its first physical floral studio and multilingual online ordering platform will begin accepting public orders in early September 2026. The opening marks the commercial debut of the IFIORA brand, its Mokotów studio and its digital storefront. Cannot view this video? Visit: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iH-K7-P4vc0 At launch, the studio and website will operate as one local business. Floral arrangements will be prepared at al. Polski Walczącej 30, unit U3/A, 00-712 Warsaw, while the online store presents ordering information in Polish, English and Russian. The service is intended exclusively for recipient addresses within Warsaw, including orders initiated elsewhere in Poland or abroad. IFIORA’s English-language storefront presents the new business, current floral formats and operating terms to English-speaking residents and international senders. Customer support is available in all three published languages. A New Studio and Online Platform Opening Together The opening will establish IFIORA as a Warsaw florist with one local studio and a citywide delivery area. Studio and support hours are Monday through Saturday, 10:00-17:00. The studio is closed on Sundays, and no Sunday delivery is offered. Preparation and delivery of an accepted order may continue after customer-facing hours until fulfilment is complete. The launch model connects digital access with physical floristry. Product descriptions, available sizes, prices and stock information appear in the online store, while florists prepare confirmed orders at the Mokotów studio. Individual product pages remain the source for the current composition, size and availability of each design. The range includes hand-tied bouquets, roses, flower boxes, flower baskets, single-variety arrangements, birthday flowers, wedding flowers, funeral and sympathy pieces, potted plants and selected accessories. Seasonal supply changes throughout the year, so a flower variety, stem count or design is treated as available only when displayed for purchase or confirmed for an accepted order. Hand-arranged bouquets are available for birthdays, anniversaries, weddings, expressions of thanks, sympathy and occasions without a formal label. Standard wrapping and a greeting card carrying the sender’s message are included with a confirmed floral order at no additional charge. Chocolates and balloons are optional paid additions when available. IFIORA purchases flowers frequently in small batches from trusted suppliers and prepares arrangements locally. Eligible fresh-flower orders are covered by a seven-day freshness guarantee when the applicable care conditions are followed. Product-specific details and the terms displayed at the time of purchase remain controlling. To view an enhanced version of this graphic, please visit: https://images.newsfilecorp.com/files/12530/313195_b187e576a4b949c7_001full.jpg Warsaw-Only Delivery Terms Published at Launch The launch includes standard and express options documented on the English page for flower delivery in Warsaw . The company delivers throughout Warsaw but does not deliver beyond the city boundary. Orders may originate in any country, but every recipient address must remain within Warsaw. Standard delivery usually takes three to four hours after an order has been accepted. The standard fee is 29 zł for an order below 500 zł, while standard delivery is free for an order valued at 500 zł or more. The stated duration is an estimate rather than an exact-time guarantee. Same-day flower delivery may be available when an order is accepted before 16:00, Monday through Saturday. Eligibility depends on the selected arrangement, flower availability, a confirmed delivery slot and current studio capacity. Submission before the cut-off does not independently guarantee same-day fulfilment. Express delivery of up to two hours costs 50 zł and requires advance contact or prior arrangement. The recipient address, required flowers and current capacity must be confirmed before the express option is accepted. Express delivery is not an automatically available checkout method and is not guaranteed at all times. Public-holiday availability requires separate confirmation. Delivery may serve homes, workplaces, hotels, restaurants, ceremony venues and other suitable addresses within Warsaw. The same city boundary, pricing rules and confirmation requirements apply across the capital. To view an enhanced version of this graphic, please visit: https://images.newsfilecorp.com/files/12530/313195_b187e576a4b949c7_002full.jpg English Access for International Senders The English storefront supports residents who prefer English and people arranging flowers from outside Poland for a recipient in Warsaw. A dedicated guide explains how to send flowers to Warsaw from abroad, including the local-address requirement, ordering sequence, delivery fees, time conditions and included items. An overseas sender may select an arrangement shown as available, provide the recipient’s Warsaw address, add a greeting-card message and use a delivery option displayed or confirmed for that order. The arrangement is then prepared in Mokotów and delivered locally. IFIORA accepts international orders but does not claim international flower delivery, because the flowers themselves remain within Warsaw. English and Russian access accompany the Polish storefront so that operational information can be reviewed before an order is accepted. Each language version communicates the same citywide boundary, studio schedule, conditional same-day rule, express-confirmation requirement and basic fee structure. According to IFIORA, the opening was designed around one local operating structure: a Mokotów studio, arrangements prepared by florists, three-language information and delivery terms confirmed for each order. Multilingual ordering broadens access to the local service without expanding the delivery territory beyond Warsaw. To view an enhanced version of this graphic, please visit: https://images.newsfilecorp.com/files/12530/313195_b187e576a4b949c7_003full.jpg Local Preparation for Celebratory and Sensitive Occasions Every confirmed floral order is prepared at the Mokotów studio rather than forwarded to a nationwide fulfilment network. Preparation, customer communication and city delivery therefore remain within one local operation. Birthday flowers may include seasonal mixed bouquets, roses, flower boxes or baskets. Wedding flowers in Warsaw may include bridal bouquets, ceremony flowers and table arrangements developed through individual consultation. Romantic, anniversary, corporate and everyday designs provide further catalogue options, subject to live product availability. Funeral flowers in Warsaw include bouquets, wreaths, sprays and restrained compositions. Time-sensitive funeral orders require an exact Warsaw address, ceremony date and delivery information so that design and delivery-slot availability can be checked before acceptance. The form, scale and flower selection remain subject to the details confirmed for the order. A Defined Entry into Warsaw’s Florist Market IFIORA will enter the Warsaw market as an independent florist rather than a marketplace, delivery application or nationwide relay service. The first public launch establishes the brand’s physical location, online catalogue, multilingual ordering and local fulfilment model at the same time. The physical studio provides a place for floral preparation and customer support, while the online platform communicates current products and conditions. Together, they create one service for Warsaw recipients and for senders located elsewhere, with the city limit of every accepted delivery stated clearly. About IFIORA IFIORA, an independent online flower shop in Warsaw , is based in Mokotów and prepares hand-arranged bouquets and floral compositions at its local studio. The company delivers exclusively within Warsaw. Online ordering and customer support are available in Polish, English and Russian. Standard service operates Monday through Saturday under confirmed order conditions. Home Paid news feed Foto Agerpres Press Monitoring Bucharest Phone: +4 021.2076.110 PNL accuses PSD of political deal with AUR over Romanian public broadcaster leadership Category: English Date: 2026-09-08 19:19:07 Foto: SILVIU MATEI / AGERPRES FOTO The National Liberal Party (PNL) on Tuesday accused the Social Democratic Party (PSD) of 'putting public television in the hands of the Alliance for the Union of Romanians (AUR)', following a decision by the joint Standing Bureaus of the Chamber of Deputies and Senate on the appointment of interim heads of Romanian Television and public radio, namely journalist Sorina Matei and Razvan Dinca. 'PSD took an extremely serious step today: it voted for AUR's proposal for the leadership of public television. This is not simply an appointment. It is the result of a political agreement between PSD and AUR, through which the Social Democrats have decided to place one of Romania's most important information institutions in the hands of an extremist party. Today's vote confirms what we said a week ago: PSD and AUR are working together and voting for each other's people and interests. This time, however, the stakes are much higher: national television,' PNL said in a statement. The Liberals said TVR is an institution funded by all Romanians and a source of information for millions of people, adding that 'at a time when Romania borders a war and disinformation and propaganda represent real threats, control over public information cannot become the currency of a political bargain between PSD and extremist forces'. 'This is all the more serious because AUR consistently promotes anti-European messages and adopts narratives that undermine Romanians' trust in state institutions, the European Union and Romania's strategic partnerships. PSD must publicly explain why it chose to put national television in the hands of extremist forces and what it received in return. Ensuring that Romanians are properly informed is a matter of national interest and national security. TVR is not PSD's television and it is not AUR's television. It is the television of all Romanians,' PNL added. In a Facebook post, PNL MP Raluca Turcan said that, for the second time in a week, 'PSD and AUR have joined forces and divided up positions through a vote in Parliament'. 'This time, they have got their hands on TVR and public radio. PSD takes public radio, AUR takes TVR. Quite an arrangement for two parties that quarrel so convincingly in front of the cameras! If we had finally received a report from the Presidential Administration on the annulment of the presidential election and the Russian Federation's hybrid attack on Romania, on the mechanisms used to manipulate, spread propaganda and contaminate the public information space, I am convinced that AUR's new proposal for TVR would have featured prominently on that list. This is an extremely serious matter, because who runs public television and what guarantees exist for its editorial independence are issues that also concern Romania's democratic security,' Turcan said. She accused PSD and AUR of turning the two public broadcasters into 'bargaining chips in a PSD-AUR political deal', adding: 'I am increasingly convinced that what we are actually witnessing are the first episodes of a broader political bargain aimed at installing a PSD-AUR government.' The joint Standing Bureaus of Parliament on Tuesday approved new interim leadership appointments at the Romanian Television Corporation (SRTv) and Radio Romania Actualitati (RRA). Razvan Dinca was nominated president-director general of the public radio broadcaster, while journalist Sorina Matei was appointed director general and chair of the Board of Directors of SRTv. https://www.yahoo.com/news/world/article.text: Return to Homepage Top Stories: Mass shootings in South Africa leave 27 dead 'Major incident' near U.S. air base Nor'easter batters East Coast Trump's 'pocket rescission' Talarico's lead narrows White House blocks CNN Trump rejects Iran ceasefire OpenAI probes user data leak Trump cuts $1B, sets deadline ICE sweeps may hit beef prices Poland and Ukraine said Russia struck a Warsaw-bound train in west Ukraine but caused no casualties (Sergei SUPINSKY) Poland and Ukraine denounced on Sunday Russian strikes close to the Polish border that hit a Warsaw-bound train near a frontier checkpoint just after another train carrying several EU officials and British ex-PM Boris Johnson passed through. Ukraine's rail operator said Johnson and former US CIA director David Petraeus, who were in Kyiv for the annual Yalta European Strategy forum, had been travelling on two separate trains around the time the Warsaw-bound locomotive was hit. Petraeus told the New York Times in a telephone interview on Sunday that he could hear Russian drones above followed by an explosion -- prompting passengers to be quickly evacuated. Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "For those who have not been under fire, this was terrifying... This is the act of a truly barbaric leader trying to terrorise Ukrainian civilians," he added. Johnson, who was travelling with several EU officials in a separate train, condemned the attack in a post on X. "I don't know what warped logic drove Putin to blow up a stationary Ukrainian locomotive on the Polish border this morning," he said. "What we can say for sure is that this is the kind of random and senseless attack Ukrainians are enduring every day -- even on civilian railways." Poland and Ukraine said a Kyiv-Warsaw passenger train was struck just two kilometres (1.2 miles) from the Polish border, but reported no casualties. Advertisement Advertisement Warsaw has been one of Kyiv's main allies and, with Ukrainian airspace closed, trains to Poland have been one of the main routes out of the war-torn country, used by refugees. The Ukrzaliznytsia rail operator confirmed the attack on Sunday but did not say how far the officials were from the strike site. "A diplomatic train was at Yagodyn station... among others, security advisers from several EU member states and former European leaders (were) on board, including former UK Prime Minister Boris Johnson," the operator said. "In another train that was at Yagodyn station at the very moment of the attack was former CIA Director David Petraeus." Advertisement Advertisement - Escalated attacks - The strikes came as US President Donald Trump called on Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky to halt attacks on Russian refineries, saying it was causing a shortage of diesel fuel and "there are plenty of other targets". Ukraine has increasingly targeted Russian oil refineries in a bid to hurt Russia's war effort. Russia attacked western Ukraine with drones Sunday, just days after US envoys visited Kyiv and Moscow in a bid to revive talks to end the war. Zelensky said Moscow "deliberately" struck the locomotive. "It is precisely to prevent these strikes from spreading further into Europe that Ukrainian men and women fight every day, give their lives, and do not allow the aggression to expand," Zelensky said. He added: "We cannot exclude that the escalation will also affect our territory... I hope not." Russia said it had hit "railway infrastructure used to transport military cargo" from European countries. - Russia 'knocking at Europe's door' - Speaking in Kyiv, Poland's foreign minister Radoslaw Sikorski said the "escalation" should lead to allies to "double" their support for Ukraine. "This was just a few hundred meters from the Polish border, this affects the safety of my countrymen," Sikorski said. "Putin's terror is literally knocking at the door of the European Union and NATO," Sybiga said. Russian attacks killed at least two people on Sunday in the frontline city of Kramatorsk. Twenty people, including two children, were also wounded in a second day of attacks on the southern port city of Odesa, Ukrainian officials said. - Three-way talks - The Kremlin, meanwhile, said negotiations with Ukraine and the United States on the war could take place in October. "We do not rule out such a possibility; we are talking about the foreseeable future," Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told journalists, cited by Russia's Ria and Tass news agencies. https://www.politico.eu/article/france-c.text: France called on Israeli authorities to take “all necessary measures” to “stop these acts of terror” following an attack by masked Israeli settlers against European diplomats in the West Bank on Saturday. In a statement issued Sunday, the French Ministry of Foreign Affairs said: “France calls on the Israeli authorities to arrest the perpetrators of this extremely serious assault and bring them to justice. “Furthermore, the Israeli authorities must take all necessary measures to put an end to these acts of terror and to ensure the safety of civilian populations and diplomatic missions, as they are obligated to do under international law.” Advertisement Advertisement The incident took place in Taybeh, a mainly Christian town north of Jerusalem, where diplomats and other officials from France, Poland and Belgium were watching local people harvest olives. Video footage of the attack showed settlers confronting a convoy of diplomats and a man wearing a French tricolor sash slumped beside a car. “The mayor of the commune of Aulnoye-Aymeries was violently assaulted by extremist settlers in the West Bank,” French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot said on X, adding that that Israel “must urgently put an end to these criminal acts.” Belgian Foreign Minister Maxim Prévot said that in addition to the assault on the French mayor, a Belgian vehicle was damaged in the incident. He added that “Israeli authorities must protect Palestinians, ensure the safety of diplomats and journalists, and bring those responsible to justice,” and said Belgium “will continue to press for EU sanctions against those responsible for this violence and those who support them.” On Sunday morning, an EU spokesperson said that the bloc “strongly condemns” the attacks by violent settlers in the West Bank, “including on European diplomats.” The spokesperson added: “We take positive note of statements by several Israeli representatives who condemned the attacks but we expect full accountability as well as effective measures to prevent continued acts of violence and violent harassment against Palestinians, including during the ongoing olive harvest season, as well as against journalists.” Writing on X , the Israel Defense Forces strongly condemned “the severe act of violence that took place in the area of Taybeh, during which diplomatic representatives were attacked by Israeli rioters.” The IDF added that “according to a preliminary inquiry, no IDF soldiers were present at the scene at the time of the attack”. However, the office of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu urged caution “before drawing conclusions” from reports of the attack, while noting that “any violence against diplomats is unacceptable.” Advertisement Advertisement

https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/ck5y.text: Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Anti-migrant protesters in South Africa demand that all undocumented foreign nationals leave the country By Ondiro Oganga Published 4 hours ago A foreign national has been beaten to death by a crowd of about 50 people in Durban, South Africa, police say. According to police, the unidentified man, believed to be in his late 30s or early 40s, was first approached by two men by the roadside before being assaulted by a larger group. He was pronounced dead at the scene. Police have launched an investigation into the murder, with the motive yet to be established. The killing follows a wave of protests against immigrants in South Africa this year, some of which have turned violent. Earlier this month, shops and cars were set on fire in Durban, as well as Soweto, near Johannesburg. Provincial police spokesperson Robert Netshiunda told the BBC they cannot speculate on the motive for the killing in Durban and that more information would be shared once verified. 'We have to prioritise South Africans': Anti-migrant movement blocks foreigners from healthcare Published 18 October 2025 The uniformed group targeting foreigners in South Africa Published 18 September 2023 The government has urged the demonstrators to act peacefully, while also accepting the need for immigration reforms. It says tens of thousands of foreign nationals have been deported or repatriated since it launched a crackdown earlier this year. One of the groups behind the protests, March and March, had initially set a deadline of 30 June for all undocumented migrants to leave South Africa. Several protests were held ahead of that deadline, with reports of attacks on people from other African countries. These prompted several countries, including Zimbabwe, Nigeria and Ghana, to take steps to repatriate their citizens amid fears of further violence. Nigeria accused South African authorities of responsibility for the deaths of two of its citizens that month. Ghana also confirmed the death of a citizen, Bashiru Isak, a father of three who was fatally shot in Cape Town during demonstrations targeting foreign nationals. His death led to a diplomatic row with South Africa, which said the scale of the violence had been exaggerated. One of the leaders of the March and March movement, Jacinta Ngobese-Zuma, denied that she was xenophobic. "We can't be living with these people for so many years and now when we say it is too much, it is enough, we are told that we are xenophobic," she told the BBC's Focus on Africa programme. South Africa has struggled with xenophobic attacks for nearly two decades. In 2008, more than 60 people were killed and tens of thousands displaced during widespread attacks on foreign nationals. The latest unrest comes against a backdrop of widespread poverty, deep inequality and unemployment affecting roughly a third of the workforce. Migrants are frequently accused of taking jobs, contributing to crime and placing pressure on public services, although researchers say such sweeping claims are not supported by evidence. Despite its economic difficulties, South Africa remains one of the continent's main destinations for migrants seeking employment, safety and better opportunities.
